newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to send Richardson to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to send Richardson to Zaire.

text.p: Bill Richardson, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, will visit Zaire soon in an effort to get peace negotiations started, the White House announced on Saturday.
During the trip Richardson plans to meet senior leaders of the Zairian government of President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leaders trying to drive Mobutu from power.

"He will press both sides to agree to halt the fighting and launch serious negotiations to form an inclusive transitional government leading to free and fair democratic elections," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said in a statement.
Another White House official, summing up Richardson's mission, said he would attempt to get Mobutu and rebel leader Laurent Kabila to talk, to try to reach a peaceful resolution.
Kabila's rebel forces, known as the Alliance of Democratic Froces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, have seized more than half of Zaire since October.

The United States has increased pressure on Mobutu to step down to clear the way for a transitional government in Zaire but Mobutu has refused. The White House official said Richardson's mission was not to pressure Mobutu to resign.
